slides.title: Humor Style Drives Laughter, Topic Shapes Acceptability: Evaluating Bilingual Personal and Political Robot-Delivered AI Jokes
slides.highlight: This study examines how humor style and joke content affect the perceived funniness and appropriateness of robot-delivered AI jokes, contributing to the development of embodied social robots for RwB.

card.one_liner: Humor style drives perceived funniness, while joke content determines appropriateness in robot-delivered AI humor.
card.key_idea: A mixed factorial study evaluating how humor type (Affiliative, Self-Enhancing, Aggressive, Self-Defeating) and content (person-related vs. political) affect perceptions of robot-delivered jokes.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via a university classroom study measuring funniness, appropriateness, and language preference across different humor types and contents.
card.limitation: The study is described as exploratory and conducted within a specific university classroom setting.

slides.title: Pudu Robotics Unveils PuduFM 1.0 and PuduAgent
slides.tldr: NEW HUMANOID AND EMBODIED AI SYSTEMS
slides.highlight: The introduction of PuduFM 1.0 and PuduAgent advances humanoid and embodied AI systems, which is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots.

slides.title: GIVE: Grounding Human Gestures in Vision-Language-Action Models
slides.tldr: ENHANCING VLA MODELS WITH HUMAN GESTURE UNDERSTANDING
slides.highlight: GIVE improves human-robot interaction by integrating visual and semantic gesture information into VLA models to better ground intent. This is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: GIVE enhances pre-trained VLA models with human gesture understanding via visual and semantic guidance pathways.
card.key_idea: Injects hand skeleton/pointing rays as visual overlays and VLM-generated textual descriptions into VLA models without architectural changes to improve spatial grounding and intent understanding.
card.evaluation: Real-world experiments on Galaxea R1-Lite robot; improved target recognition by 40% and handover success by 80% over baseline $\pi_{0.5}$.
card.limitation: Performance may degrade under severe motion blur, occlusions, or extreme distances due to a fixed ray extension scalar.

slides.title: Hierarchical Policies from Verbal and Egocentric Human Signals for Natural Human-Robot Interaction
slides.highlight: The EDITH framework integrates first-person view, gaze, and speech to reduce user effort in human-robot interaction. This is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: EDITH enables robots to interpret human intent using combined verbal instructions and egocentric gaze/view signals.
card.key_idea: A hierarchical policy using a VLM high-level controller to produce subtasks (fine-grained instructions + keyframes) and a VLA low-level controller for execution.
card.evaluation: Tested on three HRI tasks (muffin-serving, tumbler-sorting, tool-passing); achieved 59.7% average success rate, significantly outperforming language-only baselines (<6.5%).
card.limitation: Reactivity is limited by high-level policy latency and performance degrades for users with physical attributes (e.g., height) differing from training data.

slides.title: UBTECH launches UWORLD U1 humanoid robot companions
slides.highlight: The launch of UWORLD U1 humanoid robot companions is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots.

slides.title: Data Aphasia: An Institutional Counterfactual Study of the Stability of Academic Cognition Under Letter-Grade Evaluation Systems
slides.tldr: IMPACT OF LETTER-GRADE SYSTEMS ON ACADEMIC COGNITION
slides.highlight: This study introduces 'data aphasia' to analyze how institutional data presentation restricts diagnostic information, providing insights for MIMIC's societal-scale simulation of human-AI societies and cognitive costs.

card.one_liner: Letter-grade systems cause "data aphasia," significantly reducing diagnostic stability and information compared to percentage scores.
card.key_idea: Institutional counterfactual simulation converting percentage scores to letter grades to analyze information entropy, structural stability, and diagnostic identity consistency across mathematics examinations.
card.evaluation: Tested on 68 exams from 75 primary students; found 69% entropy decrease and high sensitivity to anchor student removal.
card.limitation: The study is limited to a specific sample of primary school mathematics examinations.

slides.title: Adaptive Turn-Taking for Real-time Multi-Party Voice Agents
slides.highlight: This work introduces ModeratorLM to improve turn-taking precision and reduce interruptions in multi-party conversations, supporting HyECHO's focus on listener modeling and engagement in hybrid human-AI teams.

card.one_liner: ModeratorLM is a role-playing voice agent that adapts turn-taking behavior based on an assigned persona.
card.key_idea: A streaming speech LLM conditioned on explicit roles, featuring a reasoning-augmented variant (ModeratorLM-Think) using chain-of-thought to decide when to intervene in multi-party conversations.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on real-world meeting data (NSF-1) and synthetic RolePlayConv; showed >40% precision and >70% recall improvement over non-role-conditioned baselines.
card.limitation: The model relies heavily on textual transcriptions for decisions and can be sensitive to audio chunking strategies.

slides.title: Multi-Modal Multi-Agent Robotic Cognitive Alignment enabled by Non-Invasive Consumer Brain Computer Interfaces: A Proof of Concept Exploration
slides.highlight: This work explores a closed-loop architecture using consumer-grade BCIs to monitor human cognitive load, allowing multi-agent systems to defer communications during high mental workload. This is relevant to RwB's focus on human-robot interaction and embodied social robots.

card.one_liner: A BCI-driven framework that defers robotic agent communications during periods of high human cognitive workload.
card.key_idea: A closed-loop architecture using consumer EEG to monitor spectral band powers, triggering an HTTP signaling mechanism to queue agent messages when high engagement is detected.
card.evaluation: Proof-of-concept exploration using real-time signal processing, LLMs, and physical robots; results demonstrate the feasibility of the proposed cognitively-aware pipeline.
card.limitation: Preliminary results based on a proof-of-concept exploration; specific performance metrics and large-scale validation are not clearly stated.

slides.title: Predicting Cognitive Load from Speech and Interaction Dynamics in Dyadic Conversations
slides.tldr: COGNITIVE LOAD PREDICTION VIA SPEECH DYNAMICS
slides.highlight: This research identifies how turn-taking dynamics and participation imbalances in dyadic conversations predict cognitive load, supporting HyECHO's goals in modeling hybrid team states.

card.one_liner: Speech and interaction dynamics can predict perceived cognitive load in dyadic conversations as a regression task.
card.key_idea: A two-head GRU encoder uses static acoustic, temporal derivatives, and interaction features (e.g., turn-taking, speaking imbalance) to predict NASA-TLX cognitive load scores.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on 53 dyads (AVCAffe dataset) using Leave-One-Dyad-Out cross-validation. Metrics include CCC, PCC, and RMSE; results show modest, generalizable signals for temporal/mental demand.
card.limitation: Small sample size (475 task samples) limits deep learning capacity; results may reflect task-specific interaction patterns rather than cognitive load alone.
